clinician.final_diagnosis: DM type 2, hypertension, homozygote HbE and renal complications
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old Sumba tribe woman with 10-year history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presented for routine follow-up reporting weakness and dizziness. Initial laboratory evaluation revealed microcytic hypochromic anemia with Mentzer Index <13 and characteristic peripheral smear findings (target cells, ovalocytes, anisopoikilocytosis) suggesting hemoglobinopathy. Hemoglobin electrophoresis confirmed homozygous HbE (89.4% HbE, 2.9% HbA, 3.8% HbF, 3.9% HbA2). HbA1c testing by HPLC demonstrated analytical interference showing 'no result' with absent peaks due to HbE presence, and review of prior immunoturbidimetric HbA1c results revealed discrepancies with blood glucose levels. Iron studies were performed to evaluate for concomitant iron deficiency. The working diagnosis incorporated her known long-standing diabetes and hypertension, newly confirmed homozygous HbE as the etiology of her anemia, and renal complications.
